Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Definition and recipe reference

Look up the JSON fields and Java operations used to define a molecule. The tables list accepted values, defaults, and limits; their linked guides show complete examples. A JSON file’s namespace and path supply its molecule ID.

Calls used in the examples

When you finish: A builder creates a model but does not add it to the game. Java registrations use a name, called an owner, to group the definitions your mod controls; choose your mod ID. A RegistrationJob lets you cancel pending work or remove its installed set later. JSON and Groovy registrations use their file or script loading rules instead. Keep drawing and exports in client code.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.

Find definition files and check which one wins

Find definition files and check which one wins
Order Source Path / effect
1 Definitions included with mods data/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json
2 Java registrations AvogadroApi.owner(...)
3 Packs installed for this instance config/avogadro/packs/
4 Instance JSON config/avogadro/server/data/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json
5 Packs installed for this world <world>/avogadro/packs/
6 World JSON <world>/avogadro/data/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json
7 Script registrations GroovyScript and CraftTweaker registration sets
Client display 1 Resource-pack models assets/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json in mods, packs, server pack, then config/avogadro/resources/assets
Client display 2 Local JSON config/avogadro/molecules/<path>.json → avogadro:<path>

Later sources in the table take priority when molecule IDs overlap. The server sends its chosen definitions to clients, which can then apply local display overrides. An invalid server pack rejects the complete pack reload and keeps the previous result; ordinary non-pack definition loading can fall back to an earlier valid definition. See installing and reloading molecule packs for folder/ZIP ordering. Use lowercase descriptive ID paths such as organic/ethanol.

Molecule fields

Molecule fields
Field Type / default Meaning
name String Optional display name, 1–256 characters
formula String Optional ordinary-digit formula; otherwise derived from atoms. Generated-item composition must agree
smiles String Connectivity plus schematic layout; adds implicit H according to supported valence rules
atoms Array Every explicit atom: e, x, y, z; optional nuclear data
bonds Array [from,to] or [from,to,type]; indices start at 0. Missing means distance inference; [] disables it
structure Object Fragment recipe / assembly. Cannot coexist with copy, atoms, bonds, or smiles
copy String ID Copy a supplied definition; cycles/missing targets fail. Inherit missing fields; associations union
edits Array Ordered edits after geometry/copy resolution
materialize Boolean Required when editing a crystal/polymer preview into a finite result
polymer Object Linear chain recipe with explicit caps
polymer_network Object Parameterized network recipe, seed, algorithm version
crystal Object Cell lengths, angles, optional origin
items / fluids Selector arrays Registry IDs, item metadata, partial NBT requirements
item_tags / fluid_tags String arrays Avogadro association dictionary IDs
materials String array Optional supported legacy GregTech material IDs
match_containers Boolean; true Allow contained-fluid associations
generate_item Boolean; false Expose a sample through the shared molecule item, not a new registry item
elements Object Per-symbol neutral nuclear/shell defaults
atom_configurations Object Per-index atomic overrides; not flattened network overrides
components Array References for inspection; do not add geometry
inspection Object String-valued inspection metadata and presentation classification
Tip Choose one geometry source: copy, atoms, SMILES, structure, polymer, or polymer_network. Definitions with conflicting geometry sources are rejected. Unsupported top-level and atom/structure fields are rejected. IDs come from file paths; do not add an id field. Each resource file is limited to 256 KiB.

Supported SMILES and bonds

Supported SMILES and bonds
Chemical SMILES Formula
Water O H2O
Methane C CH4
Ethanol CCO C2H6O
Acetone CC(=O)C C3H6O
Benzene c1ccccc1 C6H6
Acetic acid CC(=O)O C2H4O2
Carbon dioxide O=C=O CO2

Supported: branches, disconnected pieces, digit/%nn ring closures, common organic/aromatic and bracket atoms, and bond symbols - = # : / \. Tetrahedral @ and @@ select three-dimensional arrangements and produce checked R/S labels; neither marker means R or S on its own. Directional double-bond markers / and \ are not supported as stereo instructions and are rejected on the stereochemical path. See mirror-image molecules for the supported cases and limits. Bracket isotope/charge syntax does not supply examiner nuclear data. Use explicit atomic configurations for that.

Supported SMILES and bonds
Bond input Type
Omitted third entry / SINGLE / 1 / - Single
DOUBLE / 2 / = Double
TRIPLE / 3 / # Triple
QUADRUPLE / 4 Quadruple

All JSON edit operations

All JSON edit operations
op Required fields Effect
replaceAtom index, e Change element; clear old atom configuration if changed
moveAtom index, x, y, z Move one atom
atom e, x, y, z Append an atom
setBond from, to; optional type Create/replace a bond
removeBond from, to Remove an edge
removeAtoms indices array Resolve all current indices, then delete and remap
append instance, structure Append a named fragment
connect from, to attachment paths; optional type Connect named atoms
attachment name, index Add an attachment
removeAttachment name Remove a name
atomConfiguration index, nuclear Assign atomic data
clearAtomConfiguration index Remove atomic data
randomLinkCapacity index, capacity Assign additional random-link capacity

At most 64 edit operations. Syntax validates immediately; geometry-dependent references validate against the resolved copy source. Each operation sees indices after previous operations.

Structure recipes and assembly JSON

Structure recipes and assembly JSON
Shape Fields / use
Base fragment atoms (optional nuclear data per atom), bonds, attachments, random_link_capacities; optional cell with vectors and links
Ordered operations translate, rotate, scale, affine, repeat, append, instances, wrapCylinder; see StructureFragment and its serialized recipe
Finite assembly structure: {assembly: {nodes: […], links: […], random_links: […]}}
Fragment node name, kind="fragment", structure, optional transform
Group node name, kind="group", body, optional transform
Repeat node name, kind="repeat", body, count (integer or parameter name), step; optional head/tail and neighbor_links
Choice node name, kind="choice", rule_id, probability (number or parameter), present/absent bodies
Explicit link from, to, type
Random link rule_id, from, to, pairing, probability, type
Network wrapper random_version=1, seed as decimal string, parameters, assembly

Use the crown assembly, PEG definition, and polyisoprene network from the guides as exact schema examples. They use the same Java builders shown in the tutorials and show the field names for advanced recipes.

Every structure operation

Every structure operation
op Fields Effect
translate by: [x,y,z] Move all atoms
scale by: number or [x,y,z] Scale coordinates
rotate axis: [x,y,z], degrees Rotate around the authored axis
affine matrix: 3 × 4 array Apply an authored affine matrix
repeat counts: 1–3 integers; optional wrap booleans Expand a unit cell; wrapping closes selected periodic boundaries
instances transforms: matrix array; optional prefix Place explicit copies and qualify names
append structure; optional instance Append a fragment, optionally with qualified names
edit edits: edit-operation array Apply the same editing contract as top-level edits
wrapCylinder circumference, axis, length; optional origin Wrap authored geometry without optimizing its chemistry

Operations execute in array order. A cell uses vectors and relative links; include a repeat operation to materialize it before returning a molecule structure. All coordinates must be finite. See the builder-serialized downloads for complete runnable recipes.

Atomic and cell objects

Atomic and cell objects
Object Fields
Atomic configuration atomic_number, neutrons, optional charge, electron_shells array
Cell a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma; optional origin_x, origin_y, origin_z
Tag dictionary replace boolean, values array of selectors or #tag references
Network count parameter name, label, kind="count", min, max, default
Probability parameter name, label, kind="probability", min=0, max=1, default

See atom details, matching rules, and network limits for validation and behavior. Export settings are listed in the export options table.

Keep display and atom data when copying

Additional root definition fields
Field Meaning
presentation Partial display values: hei_visible, hei_item_slot, creative_visible, tooltips, world_hud, polymer_preview_units. See pack settings.
molecule_tags At most 256 molecule tag identifiers; separate from item/fluid associations.
atom_isotopes Canonical zero-based atom indices mapped to exact mass numbers, 1..10000 and at least the proton count. Retains isotope-dependent stereo priorities; does not infer atom inspection configurations.
stereochemistry Canonical atom-index keys mapped to R/S strings. Explicit coordinates and graph must independently verify every assignment.

Snapshots retain these fields alongside template annotations, constraints, inspection data and bindings. Supply one structure source. Atomic/cell objects reject unknown fields and integer values must be mathematically exact.

Find elements by category

Click a category in the periodic table legend to flash its element symbols red twice. Point at a category on a wall table to see its name in HWYLA, The One Probe, The One Probe: Community Edition, or The One Smeagle. Category labels do not add a hover outline.

The probe variants share a mod ID, so install one of them. Either works alongside HWYLA. Detached Avogadro viewers use the benzene icon from the creative tab.

Look up and import CAS substances

See Commands and imports for API key setup, CAS lookup, synonyms, batch imports, and offline files. Imports use the ordinary Java molecule builder.

Enable or disable elements

Element samples and atomic viewers are enabled by default. Turn off Enable elements and atomic viewers under Elements and restart the game to omit the periodic-table item and painting entity and disable atomic examination. Use the same elements setting on the client and server, since it changes item and entity registrations. Ordinary molecule previews remain available. Isotope samples are a separate option.
